Law Passed: California SB 54 (Plastic Pollution Prevention and Packaging Producer Responsibility Act), enacted June 2022; permanent regulations effective May 1, 2026; now facing three concurrent legal challenges, including a July 14, 2026 federal court preliminary injunction blocking enforcement of companion law SB 343 that could affect SB 54 recyclability targets.
Status Detail: Final SB 54 regulations took effect May 1, 2026, triggering producer registration (due June 1, 2026) and annual supply/source reduction reporting (due May 31, 2026); the Circular Action Alliance (CAA) submitted its draft program plan for full program launch January 1, 2027. Two lawsuits filed in June 2026 challenge the SB 54 regulations — one by environmental groups in state court (June 2, 2026) and one by a 17-state coalition plus NAW in federal court (June 22, 2026) — while a separate July 14, 2026 federal preliminary injunction blocked enforcement of companion recyclability-labeling law SB 343, which SB 54 relies upon to determine what counts as 'recyclable'; no injunction has yet been issued against SB 54 itself, so all compliance obligations remain active.

Law Passed: Colorado HB22-1355 (Producer Responsibility Program for Statewide Recycling Act), signed June 2022, is now in active implementation. The program covers all packaging materials and paper products — including flexible/film packaging, bags, and paper-based materials — sold or distributed in Colorado. Producer responsibility dues began January 1, 2026. CAA's Final Program Plan was approved by CDPHE on December 9, 2025, with full statewide implementation required by June 9, 2026. A separate 2026 legislative attempt to add a formal fee-appeal mechanism failed to pass. A constitutional legal challenge (ILMA v. CDPHE) filed March 12, 2026 is pending but has not enjoined the program.
Status Detail: As of July 2026, Colorado's EPR program is in active implementation under HB22-1355. Producers of covered packaging and paper products — including films, flexible plastics, and paper materials — are prohibited from selling into Colorado unless registered with CAA and paying producer responsibility dues (due in two equal installments in January and July each year). CDPHE moved to dismiss the ILMA constitutional challenge in early June 2026; no injunction has been sought and the program continues to operate. A 2026 bill introduced by Sen. Cutter to create a formal EPR fee-appeal mechanism before the Advisory Board failed to pass before the legislature adjourned May 13, 2026.

Law Passed: No packaging EPR law has been enacted in Connecticut. Two recent bills — HB 6917 (2025 session) and HB 5151 (2026 session) — both died without passage.
Status Detail: In the 2025 session, HB 6917, which would have mandated a study on the need and viability of packaging EPR by January 15, 2027, passed the House but died on the Senate calendar on June 4, 2025. In the 2026 session, HB 5151 — introduced February 11, 2026 — would have required the state to submit proposals derived from Connecticut's waste characterization study, including EPR recommendations for consumer packaging, but it died in committee when the 2026 session ended. Connecticut has no enacted packaging EPR law and all packaging-related EPR bills must be reintroduced in 2027.

Law Passed: Hawaii HB 750 signed into law May 27, 2025, requiring the Department of Health to conduct a statewide needs assessment for packaging materials and paper products EPR; a separate full EPR bill (HB 1264) was introduced in January 2025 and carried over to the 2026 session but did not pass.
Status Detail: HB 750 is enacted law: the Hawaii Department of Health began needs assessment work on July 1, 2025, with an advisory council established to guide the process; the final assessment report is due to the Legislature by December 31, 2027. HB 1264, a separate bill that would establish a full EPR program covering all packaging types (including bags) with a volume-based producer fee, was introduced in January 2025, referred to committee, and carried over to the 2026 regular session without passing. As of the close of the 2026 legislative session (adjourned May 8, 2026), no comprehensive packaging EPR program has been enacted in Hawaii; the state remains in the needs-assessment phase.

Law Passed: Maine's packaging EPR law (LD 1541, 2021) is in active implementation. A 2025 amendment (LD 1423) signed June 20, 2025 updated the program's definitions and scope. As of June 15, 2026, Maine DEP issued its RFP for a Stewardship Organization, with proposals due August 3, 2026. The program covers all consumer packaging materials regardless of type — including plastic film/bags, paper, mesh, and other bagging — with certain exemptions for commercial, medical, hazardous, and flammable product packaging added by LD 1423.
Status Detail: Maine's EPR program (38 M.R.S. § 2146) is at Step 4 — contracting a Stewardship Organization (SO). The RFP was published June 15, 2026, with proposals due August 3, 2026; no SO has been selected yet. DEP now anticipates registration and invoicing will begin at the end of 2026, with municipal reimbursements starting at the end of 2027. Chapter 428 rules were amended in March 2026 to add Appendix A (Packaging Material Types List) and align with LD 1423 changes.

Law Passed: Maryland SB 901 (Packaging and Paper Products Producer Responsibility Plans Act) signed into law May 13, 2025; implementing regulations adopted May 5, 2026, effective May 25, 2026.
Status Detail: SB 901 covers all packaging and paper products — including primary, secondary, and tertiary packaging (encompassing poly bags, plastic film, paper bagging, mesh bags, carry-out bags, and bulk good bags) — introduced into Maryland. Law Passed: Massachusetts Senate passed S.3050 (Mass Ready Act) on April 15, 2026, which includes a statewide ban on single-use plastic carryout bags and a 10-cent fee on recyclable paper bags. The House Committee on Ways and Means advanced its own version of the bill in June 2026 but stripped the bag ban provision. The bill remains in the House with the legislative session ending July 31, 2026. Separately, two standalone packaging EPR bills (S.571 and H.926) remain pending in their respective Ways and Means committees. No comprehensive packaging EPR law has been enacted.
Status Detail: The Massachusetts Senate passed S.3050 (Mass Ready Act) 36-3 on April 15, 2026, including a statewide single-use plastic carryout bag ban and a mandatory 10-cent fee for recyclable paper bags (with exemptions for small businesses). As of mid-June 2026, the House Committee on Ways and Means advanced its own version at a reduced bonding authorization of $3.1 billion but removed the bag ban language, creating a House-Senate conflict heading into the July 31, 2026 session deadline. The Massachusetts EPR Commission issued its final report on January 15, 2026, recommending further study (a needs assessment) for packaging EPR rather than endorsing any specific bill, and the two standalone packaging EPR bills (S.571 and H.926) remain stalled in committee.

Law Passed: Rhode Island enacted H 6207 (signed June 30, 2025), a packaging and paper EPR needs assessment law; full EPR bills H.B. 7910 and S.B. 2656 introduced in February 2026 remain pending in committee.
Status Detail: H 6207, signed by Governor McKee on June 30, 2025, mandates a third-party statewide recycling and waste-management gap analysis with recommendations due December 1, 2026—it does not establish a full EPR program. Two full EPR bills, H.B. 7910 and S.B. 2656 (introduced February 27, 2026), would require producers of packaging and paper products to fund and manage recycling, composting, and reuse through a producer responsibility organization; H.B. 7910 received a committee hearing on May 27, 2026, and S.B. 2656 remained under committee review as of late June 2026, with both bills held amid concerns over infrastructure readiness and distributor costs. The needs assessment report due December 1, 2026 is expected to inform whether and how a full EPR program will be structured.

Law Passed: Washington E2SSB 5284 (Recycling Reform Act), signed into law May 17, 2025, establishes a statewide EPR program for residential packaging and paper products — including plastic, paper, metal, and glass packaging (encompassing film, bags, and other bagging formats) — codified as Chapter 70A.208 RCW. Implementation is actively underway: the July 1, 2026 producer PRO membership deadline has now passed, with Circular Action Alliance (CAA) designated as the PRO by Ecology on March 4, 2026.
Status Detail: The law became effective July 27, 2025. Ecology designated CAA as the sole PRO for the first program plan period on March 4, 2026, and the July 1, 2026 deadline for producers to join CAA or register individually has now passed. Ecology is currently in Phase 1 (rulemaking, advisory council operation, and needs assessments), with the statewide collection list due October 1, 2026 and a preliminary needs assessment due December 31, 2026.
